narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: The Fourth Branch says Math normally must rest his feet in a maiden's lap, except when war prevents it. Goewin later tells Math that his nephews attacked her while he was away and names them.

narrativeBlocks.title: Goewin speaks to Math
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Guest translation; whitespace normalized): “Math the son of Mathonwy could not exist unless his feet were in the lap of a maiden,”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The tale links a court custom with the harm done under its protection. Keep Goewin's testimony visible; do not turn the assault into a romantic subplot or erase her account.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: This is one medieval Welsh branch in the Mabinogion collection, not a universal account of Celtic law or kingship.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Compare the rule described at the opening with Goewin's own report of how it was violated.

quiz.prompt: When can Math be without a maiden holding his feet?

choices.text: Whenever he is judging a legal dispute
Only while he is travelling to Annwvyn

quiz.explanation: The branch states the condition and gives war as the exception.
